statements.impact_statement: CVE-2018-16376 is a heap-based buffer overflow in t2_encode_packet() in src/lib/openmj2/t2.c, part of OpenJPEG's old Motion JPEG 2000 library (openmj2), reported against OpenJPEG 2.3.0 in https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/issues/1127. Upstream deleted the whole openmj2 library, together with JPWL and JP3D, in https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/85a87cd505f37027c4b74363b529a1e166e32651 ('Remove obsolete components JPWL, JP3D and MJ2', first released in OpenJPEG 2.5.0), so the OpenJPEG 2.5.3 source this package is built from (Debian openjpeg2 2.5.3-2.1~deb13u2) has only the openjp2 and openjpip libraries under src/lib (https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/tree/v2.5.3/src/lib). Debian also records that it builds without MJ2 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-16376). Checked in every published build of this source in the DHI Debian repository, all four builds of 2.5.3-2.1~deb13u2 on amd64 and arm64: none of the 72 packages (libopenjp2-7, libopenjp2-7-dev, libopenjp2-tools, libopenjpip7, libopenjpip-dec-server and the dbgsym packages of all but the -dev package) contains a file with mj2 in its name, and the symbol tables of the libopenjp2 debug files and of the libopenjp2.a static archive in every build contain no function named t2_encode_packet (the openmj2 name) and none with mj2 in its name, while the same search finds openjp2's own opj_t2_encode_packet and opj_t2_encode_packets in each of them.
